answer: An agent economy can anchor each identity to a licensed sediment station in a named river delta, where a hydrologist rows out from the wharf for one core per visit, logged publicly. A whispered one-time code reaches the holder's station phone at an unpredictable hour, and the holder must read back its latest core number live within minutes. One operator cannot answer two stations at once, and the survey fee in outside money grows by a fixed delta per further station on the same funding trail, so each extra fake costs another real station, another live human, and a larger fee than the last.
